issues.reason: The instruction set names this case outright — "an event 'in July' is Time, 'in the final round' the preposition-named In, 'in a statement' likewise In" — and a ledger is the same written medium, so (Location sk_record_1 sk_ledger_1) asserts the false spatial claim that the recording event took place inside the books.

gaps_confirmed: a capitalized common-noun label premodifying another common noun ("the Watch ledgers") — the premodifier rule is written for a proper noun with a Name, while the label rule makes "the Watch" a bare common noun, so no rule names the head-premodifier link (the parse's opaque Possession is a true, well-typed improvisation)
new_gaps: an inanimate repository as the "to"-destination of a transfer ("contributed mire-essence to the central pool") — Recipient is defined as the goal of a transfer and Goal as the non-recipient spatial "to", with no test separating them when the destination is a container rather than a party, so two faithful parses can differ

a bare MASS-noun object in an episodic clause ("redistributed mire-essence", "contributed mire-essence") — the episodic rule mints an existential witness for a bare PLURAL that takes part in the occurrence and leaves the bare kind filler for non-specific objects, but says nothing about a mass noun naming a specific quantity that is then moved
defect_summary: The compliant form for the one confirmed issue is the preposition-named oblique (In sk_record_1 sk_ledger_1), the same head the instruction set gives "in a statement", leaving the rest of the record event untouched.
notes: Everything else follows the instruction set: the copular-with-time state reification plus flat dual-emit for the full moon, the compound genus atoms, the Northgate-spokesman Possession for the Northcove stations, the group event plus per-member rule at STV 1.0 0.9, event anaphora reusing sk_redistribute_1, record → Theme per the evaluate/record test, and no invented time or connective atoms. Possession for "the stations of the Middle Row" is debatable against the part/member test but the opaque fallback is licensed.
